title: Mercury: Fire TV Incident Commander
note: words_count and words_per_minute are computed from narration_text by the generator. They describe the script, not a recording.

beats.narration_text: An incident starts. Somebody asks what broke, and the first answer everyone reaches for is: what did we just deploy. Half the time that is the wrong question, and reverting on it costs an hour.
beats.visual_action: Cold open on the loaded cockpit at 1920x1080 in a desktop browser. No click yet.

beats.narration_text: Mercury answers before anyone clicks, and its most common answer is a refusal. Against eleven hundred and sixty labelled incidents it sees a real anomaly and names nobody eighty one percent of the time. The refusal says what Mercury cannot attribute and why. It never calls the deploy innocent.
beats.visual_action: Reload the page. The hero renders the correlator's verdict and the anomaly factor as the large figure. Do not click anything yet.

beats.narration_text: The refusal that matters. Several changes landed in the hour before this spike, and nothing in a metric series says which of them did it. Mercury cannot attribute this, names none of them, and the rollback stays disabled. Rolling back here would be a guess.
beats.visual_action: Press release-train. The hero reads Cannot attribute this, names the number of changes in the window, and both rollback buttons stay disabled with their reason lines visible.

beats.narration_text: It names a change only when exactly one landed in the window. And when it does, it prints its own odds: against that same corpus the commit it names is the one that caused the reading fifty two percent of the time, over one hundred and thirteen namings. The screen says so beside the name.
beats.visual_action: Press checkout-api. The hero names the commit, quotes its message, and the line under it reads the measured precision and the number of namings it was measured over.

beats.narration_text: Both halves of that answer say where they came from, next to the number rather than under the fold. The metric series is generated locally and the badge in the card reads OFFLINE FIXTURE. The commits are real, read from the checkout.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the two source badges inside the hero card beside the anomaly factor, OFFLINE FIXTURE against metric series and LIVE against commit history. Do not scroll.

beats.narration_text: The remote moves in space, not down a list. Focus jumps to the nearest control in the direction pressed, disabled controls are skipped rather than focused, and Back returns to the wall before it would ever close the application.
beats.visual_action: Press Right, Down, Down, Up, then Down to the Evidence tiles and Right to Delivery velocity, Enter and Escape. The Focused label and the BACK legend change with each press.

beats.narration_text: One screen, two kinds of truth. The velocity panel is serving a recording because no GitHub token is set, and says so. The spend panel, on a machine with credentials, is a live Cost Explorer read, and says that too.
beats.visual_action: Load DORA velocity, then scan AWS spend. Compare the OFFLINE FIXTURE badge against the LIVE aws-cost-explorer badge. Do not read live spend figures aloud.

beats.narration_text: This public path is constrained before it is convenient. It accepts only the labelled recorded fixture, selects no external dispatcher, and says on screen that approval will contact no deployment pipeline.
beats.visual_action: Go back to checkout-api. Leave the Secret field empty and press Stage rollback with the D-pad. Show DPAD_RECORD_ONLY_DEMO and external effect NONE.

beats.narration_text: Staging still mints a single-use token bound to a hash of exactly this proposal. Change the target afterwards and the token stops applying.
beats.visual_action: Show PENDING_CONFIRMATION, the payload hash, the lease countdown as the hero figure, and Confirm becoming enabled.

beats.narration_text: Governance passes, and the product says out loud what it did not do. No deployment pipeline was contacted. The token is spent, then the same remote publishes a fixed responder handoff with the facts and next step.
beats.visual_action: Press Confirm. Hold on RECORDED, no pipeline contacted, on the board, then read the output verbatim in the evidence panel, including the sentence stating no pipeline was contacted. Press Publish handoff and hold on the shared revision, facts and next step.

beats.narration_text: The source includes a normal-launch Android TV proof that installs this exact APK and replays the same D-pad journey. A receipt is claimed only after that workflow succeeds; physical hardware is optional under the event FAQ.
beats.visual_action: Cut to docs/FIRE_TV_BUILD.md and the Android TV runtime workflow. Do not show a receipt until the recorded run exists.
